headline: ATS asthma guideline recommends inhaled steroid-containing relievers over SABA alone for ages 12 and over
dek: The American Thoracic Society's new guideline strongly recommends as-needed ICS-containing relievers rather than SABA alone, based on moderate-certainty evidence.
body:
New clinical practice guidelines from the American Thoracic Society (ATS) recommend inhaled corticosteroid (ICS)-containing reliever therapy for adolescents and adults with asthma across the severity spectrum. The guidance, published in the American Journal of Respiratory and Critical Care Medicine, covers short-acting β₂-agonists (SABAs), ICS-containing relievers and maintenance-and-reliever therapy (MART). Jindal Chest Clinics Chandigarh highlighted the guideline in a post on X.

The task force included 16 asthma clinicians and researchers, 5 methodologists and a patient representative. It addressed 6 clinical questions, used systematic literature reviews and formulated recommendations with the GRADE framework.

For patients aged 12 and older at NAEPP treatment Steps 1 and 2, the panel strongly recommends as-needed ICS-SABA over SABA alone. It drew on the BEST and BATURA randomised trials, covering 2,664 participants. Compared with SABA alone, ICS-SABA lowered the risk of severe exacerbations (RR 0.55; 95% CI 0.41-0.74) and emergency department visits (rate ratio 0.43; 95% CI 0.28-0.65), and reduced systemic corticosteroid exposure. Overall adverse event rates were comparable.

The panel also strongly recommends as-needed ICS-formoterol instead of SABA alone. Across 3 trials (N=3,052), it reduced severe exacerbation risk (RR 0.46; 95% CI 0.35-0.59). The average improvement in Asthma Control Questionnaire scores stayed below the clinically meaningful threshold.

Two further recommendations are conditional and rest on low-certainty evidence. They favour as-needed ICS plus SABA, or as-needed ICS-formoterol, over scheduled ICS plus as-needed SABA. Severe exacerbation risk did not differ significantly in either comparison. For Steps 3 to 5, the panel strongly recommends ICS-formoterol as MART over maintenance ICS-LABA plus as-needed SABA.
key_quote: the panel strongly recommends as-needed ICS-SABA over SABA alone, based on moderate-certainty evidence.
